facts.value: s32 HSD_QuatLib_8037EF28(Quaternion* p, Quaternion* q, Quaternion* out, f32 t). p and q are input quaternions, out is writable output, and t is an unchecked blend parameter. Always returns zero; no normalization, valid-angle-domain, or general output-aliasing guarantee is enforced.
facts.rationale: Avoids implying every input and t produce a valid interpolated orientation; antipodal writes can alias input storage.

facts.value: Computes the quaternion dot product without clamping or input normalization. If 1+dot > 1e-10, uses spherical weights when 1-dot > 1e-10, otherwise linear weights. In the other branch it first writes (-p.y,p.x,-p.w,p.z) to out, but both subsequent t branches overwrite all four components with weighted p and q. For distinct output storage the initial orthogonal value is unused; aliasing out with either input can change later reads. t is neither bounded nor clamped, and all paths return zero.
facts.rationale: The old description omitted that the nominal orthogonal fallback is overwritten and treated one-sided threshold branches as symmetric proximity tests.

facts.value: Extracts a quaternion from the matrix's upper-left 3x3 after dividing each column by its Euclidean length. This removes positive independent column magnitudes before the rotation extraction formula. It does not validate zero columns, shear, or reflections, so arbitrary affine matrices need not yield a unit rotation quaternion.
facts.rationale: The previous scale-independent rotation claim was too broad for reflected or sheared matrices.
